newsitem.title: UK: Mideast clean tanker rates reverse slide, may rise.
newsitem.headline: Mideast clean tanker rates reverse slide, may rise.

text.p: The recent slide in medium range clean tanker rates from the Middle East appears to have ended and the fall in the Med may have bottomed out, brokers said on Friday.

Referring to medium range Middle East rates, brokers E.A. Gibson said: "The downward slide in freight rates has been halted and, if enquiry continues at present levels, rates are likely to rise in the coming week."
They said W220 was being paid for 33,000 tonnes to India.
They also reported a rise in enquiry and fixtures on long-range voyages, with rates levelling off at W195 for 55,000 tonnes from the Middle East to Japan.
"As some of the earliest available vessels have been fixed from the Mediterranean, freight levels should remain at about W195 during the coming week," Gibson said.
Brokers reported good demand for naphtha and gas oil from the Med to the Middle and Far East, with the former fetching about W260 and the latter W210 for 27,000 tonnes.

There was also fair interest in shipping unleaded gasoline transatlantic, with at least five fixtures of at least 33,000 tonnes in the last two days, although several failed, they added. Most of the fixtures were at around W230/240 for 33,000 tonnes.
The Caribbean market was slow, with 30,000 tonnes slipping to around W265 on high available tonnage, brokers said.

According to New York-based Rigos Chartering Inc, current Caribs/upcoast clean rates are above the 1996 average of W246 but have fallen sharply from last month's average of W293. -- London newroom +44 171 542 4088
